Given that $f(x)=2\cdot {4}^{x}+2\cdot {3}^{x}-2x^2+3$, find the instantaneous rate of change at $x=-1.$

{{field-1}}
question.:question/worked-solution:
Applying the formula, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}f'(x)&=\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(2\cdot {4}^{x}+2\cdot {3}^{x}-2x^2+3) \\ &=2\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}({4}^{x})+2\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}({3}^{x})-2\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(x^2)+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(3) \\ &=2({4}^{x}\ln(4))+2({3}^{x}\ln(3))-2(2x)+0 \\ &=2\ln(4)\cdot {4}^{x}+2\ln(3)\cdot {3}^{x}-4x.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the instantaneous rate of change at $x=-1$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}f'(-1)&=2\ln(4)\cdot {4}^{(-1)}+2\ln(3)\cdot {3}^{(-1)}-4(-1) \\ &=2(\frac{1}{4})\ln(4)+2(\frac{1}{3})\ln(3)-(4)(-1) \\ &=\frac{\ln{\left(4 \right)}}{2} + \frac{2 \ln{\left(3 \right)}}{3} + 4.\end{aligned}
$$

question.:question/problem:
Given that $f(x)=3\cdot {6}^{x}+3\cdot {3}^{x}-3x^2+2$, find the instantaneous rate of change at $x=2.$

{{field-1}}
question.:question/worked-solution:
Applying the formula, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}f'(x)&=\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(3\cdot {6}^{x}+3\cdot {3}^{x}-3x^2+2) \\ &=3\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}({6}^{x})+3\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}({3}^{x})-3\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(x^2)+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(2) \\ &=3({6}^{x}\ln(6))+3({3}^{x}\ln(3))-3(2x)+0 \\ &=3\ln(6)\cdot {6}^{x}+3\ln(3)\cdot {3}^{x}-6x.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the instantaneous rate of change at $x=2$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}f'(2)&=3\ln(6)\cdot {6}^{(2)}+3\ln(3)\cdot {3}^{(2)}-6(2) \\ &=3(36)\ln(6)+3(9)\ln(3)-(6)(2) \\ &=-12 + 27 \ln{\left(3 \right)} + 108 \ln{\left(6 \right)}.\end{aligned}
$$

$$
